title: Vignelli Announce — Helvetica Typographic Monument
description: A single concept word scaled to 70% of the canvas in Helvetica, tightly tracked and ranged left, with all session metadata compressed into a 10pt cluster at bottom-left. Silence is the layout — the word is the entire argument.
philosophy: This template is an act of radical reduction inherited from Unimark and the Vignelli canon: one typeface, one weight, one word, and nothing else. It refuses illustration, color blocks, and decorative hierarchy on the grounds that they dilute the signal. The room it belongs to is a symposium opener, a gallery keynote, or a cultural institution — anywhere the speaker earns authority by saying one thing with absolute conviction. Anything added would be a confession of doubt.
goodFor: Conference title slides announcing a single theme word
Brand launch moments where the name alone must carry the room
Full-bleed section dividers in long multi-chapter decks
avoidFor: Sales decks requiring logos, social proof, or testimonial blocks
Presentations where the speaker needs visible talking-point scaffolding on screen
author: harness

examples.promptCore: The slide is a typographic monument — one word at near-poster scale, carrying the full gravitational weight of the presentation's argument before a single spoken sentence arrives. Whitespace is not absence but pressure: the vast field surrounding the word functions as a held breath, amplifying rather than diluting its charge. The mood is severe, institutional, and quietly authoritative — referencing mid-century Swiss graphic systems where reduction is itself the rhetoric. Avoid any softening gesture: no gradients, no illustrative marks, no secondary visual layer that would confess uncertainty about the single statement on screen.

examples.layoutNotes: Full-bleed canvas with a single oversized word anchored ranged-left at an 8% left inset, scaled to occupy roughly 70% of total canvas width with tight tracking and no letter-spacing relief. The word's baseline rests at the optical center of the canvas — all space above and to the right is left entirely unbroken. A compressed metadata cluster (event name, presenter, date) lives flush-left in the lowest 6% of the canvas, set at minimum viable size. No rule lines, no header band, no page number, no decorative element of any kind.

examples.promptCore: The slide reads like a thesis sentence stripped to its subject: one oversized anchor word holds the visual field as an unshakeable declaration while a single compressed subordinate line hovers below it — restrained, exact, and only as long as it must be. Compositional rhythm comes entirely from scale contrast between the dominant word and the quiet supporting text, not from color geometry or illustration. The mood is symposium-austere — the empty canvas is not absence but argument. Avoid icons, gradient washes, pull-quote boxes, or any element that implies the type needs assistance.

examples.layoutNotes: 12-column grid, content left-ranged from column 1 through column 9 with a consistent breathing outer margin on all four sides — no edge-to-edge bleed. The primary concept word sits at vertical center-high (roughly the upper 55% of the slide height), scaled to dominate; a single subordinate line — short phrase, stat, or attribution — falls immediately beneath it, separated by tight leading alone with no inserted rule. A compressed metadata cluster (section label, folio number) is pinned hard to bottom-left; no header band, no footer band, no decorative fills of any kind.
